title: Block: Memoized Recursion (Top-Down DP)
oneLiner: Count the paths through a grid moving only right or down, caching each subproblem so it is solved once.
keyTakeaway: Top-down DP is the plain recursion plus three lines: check the memo, compute, store. Key the memo on exactly the arguments that change.
explanation:
A robot starts at the top-left cell of a rows by cols grid and moves only right or down. Return how many different paths reach the bottom-right cell. A 3 by 7 grid has 28.

The number of ways into cell (r, c) is the ways into the cell above plus the ways into the cell to the left, and any cell in the top row or left column has exactly one. Written as plain recursion that is exponential, because the same cells are recomputed over and over. Add a memo keyed on (r, c): return the stored answer if there is one, otherwise compute and store. Each cell is then solved once. Climbing Stairs, Decode Ways and Word Break start as this block.

starterCode.python:
def count_paths(rows, cols):
    # 1. Make an empty memo map from (row, col) to its answer.
    # 2. Write ways(r, c): a cell in the top row or left column has exactly 1 way.
    # 3. If (r, c) is in the memo, return the stored answer.
    # 4. Otherwise ways(r - 1, c) + ways(r, c - 1); store it in the memo and return it.
    # 5. Return ways(rows - 1, cols - 1).
    return 0

gotchas: Checking the memo after recursing instead of before, which keeps the exponential running time.
A memo key that leaves out one of the changing arguments, so different subproblems share an answer.

complexity.note: Each of the rows times cols cells is computed once with O(1) work; the memo holds every cell and the recursion is at most rows + cols deep.
